ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$, and $AE$ bisects $\angle BAD$ and intersects $BC$ at point $E$. Connect $OE$. If $\angle EAO = 15^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle COE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore$ AD $\parallel$ BC, AC = BD, OA = OC, OB = OD, $\angle$BAD = $90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ OA = OB, $\angle$DAE = $\angle$AEB, \\
Since AE bisects $\angle$BAD, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BAE = $\angle$DAE = $45^\circ$ = $\angle$AEB, \\
$\therefore$ AB = BE, \\
Since $\angle$EAO = $15^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BAC = $45^\circ + 15^\circ$ = $60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$BAO is an equilateral triangle, \\
$\therefore$ AB = OB, $\angle$ABO = $\angle$AOB = $60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OBC = $90^\circ - 60^\circ$ = $30^\circ$, $\angle$BOC = $180^\circ - 60^\circ$ = $120^\circ$, \\
Since AB = OB = BE, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BOE = $\angle$BEO = $\frac{1}{2}$($180^\circ - 30^\circ$) = $75^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$COE = $120^\circ - 75^\circ$ = $\boxed{45^\circ}$, \\

推理：按坐标法设A=(0,a), B=(0,0), C=(b,0), D=(b,a)。因为ABCD是矩形，所以∠BAD=90°，且AE平分∠BAD。于是AE从A出发沿右下方45°方向，斜率为-1，与BC即y=0相交于E=(a,0)。对角线交点O是AC中点，所以O=(b/2,a/2)。

从A看，AE的方向是相对水平向右方向向下45°；AO与AC同方向，向量为(b,-a)，所以AO相对水平向右方向向下arctan(a/b)。已知∠EAO=15°，因此45°-arctan(a/b)=15°，得到arctan(a/b)=30°，所以a/b=tan30°=1/√3，即b=√3a。

现在从O计算方向。向量OC=C-O=(b/2,-a/2)=a(√3/2,-1/2)，其方向为水平向右下方30°。向量OE=E-O=(a-b/2,-a/2)=a(1-√3/2,-1/2)。其斜率对应的倾角满足tanθ=(1/2)/(1-√3/2)=2+√3=tan75°，所以OE方向为水平向右下方75°。因此∠COE是这两个方向之间的夹角：75°-30°=45°。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$, and $AE$ bisects $\angle BAD$ and intersects $BC$ at point $E$. Connect $OE$. If $\angle EAO = 15^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle COE$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle, 
$\therefore$ $AD \parallel BC$, $AC = BD$, $OA = OC$, $OB = OD$, and $\angle BAD = 90^\circ$. 
$\therefore$ $OA = OB$, and $\angle DAE = \angle AEB$. 
Since $AE$ bisects $\angle BAD$, 
$\therefore$ $\angle BAE = \angle DAE = 45^\circ = \angle AEB$. 
$\therefore$ $AB = BE$. 
Since $\angle EAO = 15^\circ$, 
$\therefore$ $\angle BAC = 45^\circ + 15^\circ = 60^\circ$. 
$\therefore$ $\triangle BAO$ is an equilateral triangle. 
$\therefore$ $AB = OB$, and $\angle ABO = \angle AOB = 60^\circ$. 
$\therefore$ $\angle OBC = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$, and $\angle BOC = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$. 
Since $AB = OB = BE$, 
$\therefore$ $\angle BOE = \angle BEO = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - 30^\circ) = 75^\circ$. 
$\therefore$ $\angle COE = 120^\circ - 75^\circ = \boxed{45^\circ}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure is a horizontally placed rectangle ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. The two diagonals AC and BD intersect at point O inside the rectangle; from A, line segment AE is drawn toward the bottom side BC, with E on BC; OE is also connected in the figure. Given that AE bisects ∠BAD, and ∠EAO=15°.

Then reason: Because ABCD is a rectangle, ∠BAD=90°, AD∥BC; the diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so OA=OB. AE bisects ∠BAD, therefore ∠BAE=∠DAE=45°. Also because AD∥BC, ∠DAE=∠AEB=45°, hence in triangle ABE, ∠BAE=∠AEB, so AB=BE. It is known that ∠EAO=15°, therefore ∠BAO=∠BAE+∠EAO=45°+15°=60°. In triangle AOB, OA=OB, and ∠BAO=60°, so triangle AOB is an equilateral triangle, thus AB=OB, and ∠ABO=∠AOB=60°. Therefore ∠OBE=90°−60°=30°. Also because A, O, C are collinear, ∠BOC=180°−∠AOB=180°−60°=120°. From AB=BE and AB=OB, obtain OB=BE, so triangle OBE is an isosceles triangle, with vertex angle ∠OBE=30°, hence ∠BOE=∠BEO=(180°−30°)/2=75°. Therefore ∠COE=∠BOC−∠BOE=120°−75°=45°.
